# Preliminary Results: key numbers (generated by analysis/01_preliminary_results.py)

## Data caveat: what these results mean

All results are **demonstrated reliability from the qualification test data in our parameter table**
(test temperature, hours, sample size, failures). The calculation is verified (it reproduces the course
chi-square formula and TI's published FITs), but a part's result only reflects the test data we
transcribed. For four parts the manufacturer's published FIT rests on other or more data than our table:

- **Renesas RH850:** only one 231-device HTOL test is in the table. Renesas's verified published FIT
  (0.0011) rests on much more data, so the RH850 is very likely **more reliable than our result shows**
  (our 60% FIT at 55 C is 15.5).
- **ADI LTC6811-1, ADuM141E, ADuM4135:** our table gives them **lower** FITs (0.32-0.45 at 55 C, 60%)
  than ADI publishes (11-34; LTC6811-1 verified, ADuM4135 not found in ADI's report, ADuM141E not
  checked), so their results **may be optimistic**.

So the supplier comparisons in the MCU, BMS AFE, digital isolator and gate driver slots, and the "least
reliable" combination built from these parts, compare the evidence in our table, not settled true
reliability. No supplier difference is statistically significant (Preliminary Results, 9b).

Condition: 55 C, mission 2,920 h, target R >= 0.999 with 95% confidence; 5,000 Monte Carlo draws, seed 5300. Library parts used as candidates (one per family).

## Supplier comparison per slot (Table 2)
- ECU MCU: F280049CPZQR vs R7F7016903AFP-C: the alternative's failure rate is 2.44x TI's (95% CI 0.07-115.19); P(TI is the more reliable) = 0.70
- BMS AFE: BQ79656PAPRQ1 vs LTC6811-1: the alternative's failure rate is 2.86x TI's (95% CI 0.08-112.33); P(TI is the more reliable) = 0.74
- Digital isolator: ISO7741QDWRQ1 vs ADuM141E: the alternative's failure rate is 3.65x TI's (95% CI 0.29-110.00); P(TI is the more reliable) = 0.85
- Gate driver: UCC21750QDWRQ1 vs ADuM4135: the alternative's failure rate is 2.67x TI's (95% CI 0.07-99.39); P(TI is the more reliable) = 0.73

## System (Table 3)
- Most reliable: F280049CPZQR + BQ79656PAPRQ1 + ISO7741QDWRQ1 + TMP4719QDGSRQ1 + UCC21750QDWRQ1 + TMCS1101A4UQDRQ1: system FIT 7.02 (95% CI 1.08-38.23); R(2,920 h) = 0.999979 (95% lower bound 0.999913); meets target: yes; 0.021 failures per 1,000 vehicles (95% CI 0.003-0.112)
- Least reliable: R7F7016903AFP-C + LTC6811-1 + ADuM141E + TMP4719QDGSRQ1 + ADuM4135 + TMCS1101A4UQDRQ1: system FIT 14.31 (95% CI 1.83-108.60); 0.042 failures per 1,000 vehicles; meets target: yes
- P(most reliable combination is truly the best of all 16) = 0.32

## Temperature sweep (Figure 2)
- most reliable system meets the target up to 90 C; fails from 95 C
- least reliable system meets the target up to 75 C; fails from 80 C

## Profile vs mean temperature
- profile 40/70/105 C at 50/30/20%: system FIT 45.09; its mean temperature, 62 C: 11.82 (3.8x higher on the profile)

## Sensitivity (Figure 3), median failures per 1,000 vehicles, most reliable system
- Operating temperature 45 / 65 C: 0.009 / 0.043 (base 0.021)
- Mission 1,460 / 5,840 h (half / double): 0.010 / 0.041 (base 0.021)
- Prior Jeffreys / uniform (base): 0.008 / 0.021 (base 0.021)
- Monte Carlo seed (5 other seeds): 0.020 / 0.021 (base 0.021)
- Ea fixed at 0.7 / independent per part: 0.021 / 0.022 (base 0.021)

## Validation (Table 4)
- Published FIT reproduced within 2x for 6 of 6 TI families (C2000 6.17 vs 6.19); published FIT inside the simulator's 95% CI for all of them
- Coverage (1,000 synthetic suppliers, realistic world): upper 97.5% bound 99.8%; central 95% interval 37% (< 0.1 expected failures), 94% (0.1-1 expected failures), 96% (1-10 expected failures), 95% (> 10 expected failures)
- P(B outlasts A) Brier score: 0.12 (model-consistent world), 0.19 (realistic world); a coin flip is 0.25
